## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Paccayatākathā* (Kv 15.1) is a section of the *Kathāvatthu*, the fifth treatise of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Catalog; SuttaCentral]. In modern scholarship on early Abhidharma literature, Dhammadinna highlights the *Paccayatākathā* alongside the *Paṭṭhāna*'s *Paccayaniddesa* as an exemplary development of the theme of causal webs within the Theravāda tradition [Dhammadinna]. SuttaCentral records one translation in one language [SuttaCentral].
While SuttaCentral does not record any curated parallels for this text [SuttaCentral], DharmaNexus identifies extensive Pali-internal text reuse (1,186 matching segments across 43 Pali texts), overwhelmingly connecting it to the *Paṭṭhāna* [DharmaNexus]. Its largest reuse partners include the *Kusalattika* (Patthana 1.2; 91 matches, longest §14.1–15.4), the *Piṭṭhiduka* (Patthana 2.13; 101 matches, longest §14.1–14.3), the *Hetugocchaka* (Patthana 2.1; 91 matches), the *Nikkhepavāra* (Patthana 1.1; 42 matches), the *Saññojanagocchaka* (Patthana 2.4; 61 matches), the *Kilesagocchaka* (Patthana 2.12; 53 matches), and other *duka* and *tika* sections [DharmaNexus]. Passages are also shared with the *Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā* and the *Visuddhimagga* [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language machine alignments, DharmaNexus detects minor matches with the Tibetan translation of the *Abhidharmakośabhāṣyaṭīkā Tattvārtha* (D4421) [DharmaNexus].
